title: Annual scientific production
what: Number of corpus documents per publication year, with compound annual growth rates.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Counts of M$PY; growth from full years only. Table: tables/ OA02_annual_production .csv
caution: Growth reflects what the search rules and the databases capture, and recent years are inflated by preprints that older years lack; it is not a clean measure of the field's true growth.

title: Average citations per year
what: Mean total citations per document divided by years since publication, for each publication year.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Citations = database citation count at the pull date; citable years = 2026 - PY + 1.
caution: A few very highly cited papers drive the peaks; years with few documents are unstable (point size shows n).

title: Most relevant sources
what: The 20 venues (journals, conferences, preprint servers) with the most corpus documents.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Source = venue string as supplied by the database, upper-cased.
caution: Venue names are not fully harmonised (workshops and proceedings volumes can be split or merged), and a preprint server counts as one 'source'.

title: Bradford's law
what: Sources ranked by productivity; the shaded core zone holds about one third of all documents.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::bradford(); zones in tables/ OA04_bradford_zones .csv
caution: Bradford zones describe concentration only; a 'core' source is the most frequent, not necessarily the best or the most relevant.

title: Source dynamics
what: Cumulative number of corpus documents over time in the eight most frequent sources.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::sourceGrowth(top = 8, cdf = TRUE).
caution: A steep recent line for a preprint server partly reflects papers that have not yet appeared in their final venue.

title: Most productive authors
what: Authors with the most documents in the corpus (each co-author counted once per paper).
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Author strings 'SURNAME INITIALS' built from database author names; table also gives fractional counts and citations.
caution: Authors are matched by surname and initials only, so different people with the same short name are merged and one person with name variants is split.

title: Most cited authors
what: Authors ranked by the summed global citation counts of their documents in the corpus.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Sum of database citation counts over each author's corpus papers; every co-author receives the full count.
caution: One heavily cited multi-author paper lifts all of its co-authors; this is not a measure of individual contribution.

title: Lotka's law
what: Share of authors by number of corpus documents, against the inverse-square law.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::lotka(); table in tables/ OA06_lotka .csv
caution: A good fit says only that most authors appear once; name ambiguity (see author caption) distorts the tail.

title: Authors' production over time
what: For the 15 most productive authors: bubble size = documents that year, colour intensity = citations per year.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::authorProdOverTime(k = 15).
caution: Same name-matching caveat as the author ranking; a gap in a line may be a missing record, not inactivity.

title: Most relevant affiliations
what: Institutions appearing on the most corpus documents (once per document).
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Affiliation/country data exist for 80% of documents (400 of 497). Institution names as disambiguated by the source database.
caution: Coverage is partial and uneven: preprints and workshop papers often carry no affiliation in the database, so institutions that publish mainly that way are under-counted.

title: Corresponding-author countries
what: Documents by country of the corresponding (or first) author, split into single-country and multi-country papers.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Affiliation/country data exist for 80% of documents (400 of 497). Country from the institution country codes in the database.
caution: Only documents with affiliation data are counted, so shares are of the covered subset, not of the whole corpus.

title: Country collaboration map
what: Countries shaded by number of documents; red links join countries whose authors co-sign documents.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Affiliation/country data exist for 80% of documents (400 of 497). bibliometrix::biblioNetwork(collaboration, countries); links table in tables/.
caution: Countries with no affiliation data in the database appear empty even if they publish in this field; a link is co-authorship, not funding or influence.

title: Most globally cited documents
what: Corpus documents with the most citations from anywhere in the database.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Citation count as reported by the source database at the pull date.
caution: Global citations reward age and breadth: a general-purpose model or benchmark paper outranks a narrowly relevant study.

title: Most locally cited documents
what: Documents most cited by other documents inside the corpus - the field's own reference points.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Local citations counted by exact database identifiers where available (column LCS_exact_id_match); bibliometrix::localCitations() string matching is reported alongside as a cross-check.
caution: Local counts depend on reference lists being available: documents whose citing papers have no reference list in the database are under-counted.

title: Most cited references
what: The works the corpus cites most often, including works outside the corpus (the field's knowledge base).
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::citations(field = 'article') over the reference strings.
caution: Method and tool papers (models, toolkits, metrics) dominate such lists because nearly everyone cites them; frequency is not topical closeness.

title: Reference publication year spectroscopy
what: How many cited references were published in each year, and where that count jumps above its 5-year median (labelled peaks = historical roots).
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::rpys(timespan 1950-2026, centred median window).
caution: In a fast field almost all references are from the last few years, so the curve mostly mirrors the field's own growth; only the early, isolated peaks point to roots.

title: Most frequent keywords
what: The 30 most frequent OpenAlex keywords.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Field ID; coverage 100%. OpenAlex keywords are assigned by an algorithm from title and abstract, not chosen by the authors.
caution: Keyword counts depend on who assigned them: algorithmic keywords are consistent but coarse, author keywords are precise but unstandardised.

title: Keyword word cloud
what: The 120 most frequent OpenAlex keywords; size proportional to document count.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). wordcloud::wordcloud(), seed 42.
caution: A word cloud shows frequency only; position and colour carry no meaning, and long terms look bigger than short ones at equal counts.

title: Keyword treemap
what: Area of each tile = number of documents carrying the keyword (top 40).
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). treemapify::geom_treemap().
caution: Documents carry several keywords, so areas overlap in meaning and do not sum to the corpus.

title: Trend topics
what: For each year, the keywords whose median year of use falls there; bubble size = frequency, bar = interquartile range of years.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::fieldByYear(n.items = 4).
caution: A term placed in a recent year is 'recent on average', not necessarily new: older steady terms can be hidden by the per-year cap of four items.

title: Keyword co-occurrence network
what: Keywords (nodes, sized by frequency) linked when they appear on the same document; colours are Louvain communities.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). biblioNetwork(co-occurrences), association-strength normalisation, top 60 nodes, edges with at least 2 co-occurrences, Fruchterman-Reingold layout, seed 123.
caution: Clusters change with the number of nodes, the normalisation and the random seed; read them as a rough grouping, not a fixed taxonomy.

title: Thematic map
what: Keyword clusters placed by centrality (links to other clusters) and density (internal cohesion): motor, niche, basic and emerging/declining themes.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::thematicMap(n = 250 keywords, minfreq = 5 per thousand documents, Louvain, seed 1234); cluster table in tables/.
caution: Quadrant positions are relative ranks within this corpus only; a cluster near an axis can switch quadrant with a small change in settings.

title: Thematic evolution
what: Keyword clusters in each time slice and how they flow into clusters of the next slice (line width = share of shared keywords). Interactive version: same name .html; per-slice thematic maps: thematic_map_sliceN.png.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::thematicEvolution(cut years 2021, 2024, n = 250, minFreq = 5, Louvain, seed 1234).
caution: Cut years are a choice; early slices hold few documents, so their themes rest on small numbers and the flows from them are fragile.

title: Co-citation network of references
what: Cited works (nodes) linked when corpus documents cite them together; clusters approximate the intellectual bases of the field.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). biblioNetwork(co-citation, references) on references cited at least twice; top 60 nodes, edges with at least 3 co-citations, Louvain, Fruchterman-Reingold.
caution: Only documents with a reference list in the database contribute, and reference strings are matched by first author, year and source, so variants of one work can appear as two nodes.

title: Co-citation network of sources
what: Venues (nodes) linked when works published in them are cited together by corpus documents.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). metaTagExtraction(CR_SO) then biblioNetwork(co-citation, sources); top 40 nodes.
caution: Source names come from cited-reference strings and are unharmonised; 'ARXIV' is a single huge node that pulls everything towards it.

title: Bibliographic coupling
what: Corpus documents linked when their reference lists overlap; clusters are current research fronts.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). biblioNetwork(coupling, references), Salton normalisation, top 60 nodes, Louvain.
caution: Coupling favours documents with long reference lists (surveys) and ignores documents whose references are missing from the database.

title: Historiograph (direct citation network)
what: The 25 most locally cited documents arranged by year, with arrows for direct citations between them.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::histNetwork(min.citations = 6) and histPlot(n = 25).
caution: The picture keeps only 25 nodes; an absent arrow can mean a missing reference list rather than no intellectual link.

title: Author collaboration network
what: Authors linked by co-authorship; clusters are research groups.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). biblioNetwork(collaboration, authors); top 60 authors; isolates removed.
caution: Short author names merge namesakes, which can create false bridges between groups.

title: Institution collaboration network
what: Institutions linked when their authors co-sign documents.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Affiliation/country data exist for 80% of documents (400 of 497). biblioNetwork(collaboration, universities); top 50.
caution: Built only from the documents that carry affiliations in the database (see coverage); absent institutions are not necessarily inactive.

title: Country collaboration network
what: Countries linked by internationally co-authored documents.
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). Affiliation/country data exist for 80% of documents (400 of 497). biblioNetwork(collaboration, countries); top 35; circle layout.
caution: Same coverage limit as the country map; large countries sit in the centre because they publish more, not because they 'lead'.

title: Three-field plot (interactive HTML)
what: Sankey diagram linking author countries (left), keywords (middle) and sources (right).
how: Corpus: OpenAlex rebuild: fintech AND green finance, 2021-2026 (n = 497 documents, 2021-2026). bibliometrix::threeFieldsPlot(n = 12, 15, 12). Saved as HTML because the plotly widget cannot be rendered to PNG without a browser.
caution: Only the top items of each field are shown, so flows describe the most frequent combinations, not the whole corpus.
